ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A spherical ice droplet falls through an atmospheric layer with a temperature inversion (see Figure 1). The droplet melts partially in the warmer layer between heights $h_A$ and $h_B$, and then partially freezes again before reaching the ground. Assume constant droplet size and atmospheric density, leading to constant fall velocity. The temperature profile is linear below 2 km. Specific heat of water is $c_{\text{water}} = 4.2 \, \text{kJ kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$ and specific heat of ice is $c_{\text{ice}} = 2.1 \, \text{kJ kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}$. The specific latent heat for melting of ice is $L = 334 \, \text{kJ kg}^{-1}$. The area between the temperature curve and the height-axis in the melting region is $A = 5.0 \, \text{km} \cdot \text{°C}$, and the area in the freezing region is $A' = 4.0 \, \text{km} \cdot \text{°C}$.
<img_4520>
Figure 1: Atmospheric temperature $T$ vs. height $h$ above the ground.

1. Determine the mass fraction of the droplet that freezes before reaching the ground. 
(Note: There are no mathematical expressions in the provided text to convert to LaTeX format.)
2. Find, as precisely as possible, the temperature of the droplet at ground level if there were no inversion and the temperature profile followed the dashed line below a height of $2$ km. Neglect evaporation, condensation and size changes of the droplet. Assume that water and ice have very high thermal conductivity and that the density of the atmosphere is constant with height.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is temperature T/°C, and the vertical axis is height h/km. The black vertical axis corresponds to T=0. The blue solid line represents the temperature profile when there is a temperature inversion: it passes through T=0 near the marked h_A, then between h_A and h_B it lies to the right of T=0, that is, the temperature is higher than 0°C; at h_B it returns to T=0 again; below h_B the blue solid line lies to the left of T=0, that is, the temperature is lower than 0°C. A blue dashed line is also drawn in the figure, representing the linear extension below 2 km when there is no temperature inversion; it approximately extends from (T,h)=(4°C,2 km) to T≈8°C at the ground h=0. Reasoning: Since the problem states that the droplet size, air density, and falling speed are constant, and that during the phase-change process the droplet temperature can be regarded as 0°C, the heat exchange per unit time or per unit height differs only by a common proportionality coefficient. Therefore the heat absorbed in the melting region is proportional to the area A between the temperature curve and the T=0 axis, and the heat released in the freezing region is proportional to the corresponding area A'. Melting and solidification use the same latent heat L, so the mass fraction refrozen is the ratio of areas: η=A'/A=4.0/5.0=0.80. If there is no temperature inversion, read the ground temperature according to the dashed linear temperature profile in the figure. The dashed line intercepts at about T=8°C at h=0. Therefore, according to this method, the temperature when the droplet reaches the ground is taken to be about 8°C.
